SEND / Learning support
Heathside Walton-on-Thames caters for the range of educational needs of all its students. The Learning Support Department co-ordinates provision for students with additional needs and special educational needs and disabilities.

The Learning support department works with all members of school staff to actively progress the development of students with Special Educational and additional needs. The department aims to promote learning strategies and teaching approaches which allow these needs to be met. Support is given to teachers to enable them to provide appropriate challenges and opportunities for success for identified students. Absence Reporting and Attendance
As a school, we place a high priority on attendance as it has a marked impact on learning and academic achievement. Please see the table below explaining the impact of attendance on lessons missed.
9.5 days of absence Almost two weeks of learning missed
19 days of absence 3 weeks and 4 days of learning missed
28.5 days missed 5 weeks and 3.5 days of learning missed
38 days of absence 7 weeks and 3 days of learning missed This is the equivalent of an entire half-term
*These calculations are approximate based on a full 190 days of the academic year for years 7-10. A student’s individual timetable may vary and internal or external school events will have an impact.
We do recognise, however, that a student’s absence due to an illness or a medical appointment can be unavoidable.
Parents must notify the school on the first day of an unplanned absence – for example, if their child is unable to attend due to ill health – as soon as practically possible.
We encourage parents to make medical and dental appointments out of school hours where possible. Where this is not possible, the student should be out of school for the minimum amount of time necessary. The school will not authorise more absence than is required to attend the appointment.
Absence Reporting
If you wish to report a student absence, please leave a message as early as possible on the first day of absence and each subsequent day.
Please can you report the absence on Edulink or dial the school number (01932 955755). Please note that it is possible to leave a voicemail message when the switchboard is unmanned.
Planned Absence Request
On occasion it may be necessary for a parent to request a planned absence, such as special family occasions, work experience or a supervised sporting activity. These should be made by filling in the Absence Request Form available via your child’s Edulink account, prior to the leave date and, where possible, at least two weeks before.
All requests for absence of leave will be considered but unless there are exceptional circumstances, the absence will be unauthorised. Each request will be considered separately, and a decision made based on the reasons for each request. Requests for holidays in term time will never be authorised. For further information, please see our attendance policy.
Attendance Policy Students (heathsidewalton.org)

Careers, Education and Guidance
Welcome to Heathside Walton-on-Thames School’s student careers hub. We hope that the information provided here will support you with any questions you may have about careers and be an excellent source of information throughout your time at Heathside Walton-on-Thames.
You will find our careers policy here which details our careers provision for students.
Provider Access Legislation
Heathside Walton-on-Thames is committed to ensuring there is an opportunity for a range of education and training providers to access students, for the purpose of informing them about approved technical education qualifications and apprenticeships. Heathside is fully aware of the responsibility to set students on the path that will secure the best outcome which will enable them to progress in education and work and give employers the highly skilled people they need. That means acting impartially, in line with the statutory duty, and not showing bias towards any route, be that academic or technical.
Heathside endeavours to ensure that all students are aware of all routes to higher skills and are able to access information on technical options and apprenticeships (The Department of Education, July 2021: “Baker Clause”: supporting students to understand the full range of education and training options, and the Provider Access Legislation, January 2023).
For more information about provider access please see our careers policy.
Staff
Mr Lebihan is our Careers Lead at Heathside Walton. Parents, students and staff can contact Mr Lebihan (tlebihan@heathsidewalton.org) to seek further information on careers and destinations.
Labour Market Information
LMI is a useful source of information gathered from all regions across the UK and provides students with up-to-date statistics on careers and industry sectors within each region.
Please click here to access the latest Labour Market information shared by The National Careers Service.
Apprenticeships
At Heathside Walton-on-Thames we will ensure we provide students with up-to-date information about apprenticeships and will work closely with Year 11 students who are wanting to pursue this option.

pageCache.text:
C’était Parfait: Year 8’s French Adventure
On 5th May 104 Year 8 students left Walton for the sunny shores of la belle France for a four-day residential.
We stayed in eco-pods in the grounds of a beautiful chateau half-way between Paris and Calais.
On one day we visited Paris, went up to the very top of the Eiffel Tower and walked around the centre of Paris, spotting all the famous sights we had been learning about in lessons.
On another day, we stayed in the chateau and were taught to play pétanque and volleyball as well as how to make crèpes, all in French by some very enthusiastic and fun French animateurs.
Each evening, we practised our French, at a tuck shop or by doing obstacle courses and Olympic-style games with our French-speaking animateurs.
On the final day we went to Étaples market and saw a fabulous and traditional French market. Lots of high-quality produce was bought by all. Another highlight was going to the local French supermarket and stocking up on baguette and Sirop de Fraise or Grenadine! Thanks to the 11 staff who came on the trip and thanks to the students, who made it such fun.
Thanks also must go to the French weather, for holding off the rain and giving us lovely sunshine without too much heat! C’était parfait.

Modern Foreign Languages
Key Stage 4 Modern Foreign Languages
What is in the course?
French and Spanish are offered at Heathside Walton-on-Thames as GCSE courses. Students must choose at least one Modern Foreign Language. There are three language lessons per week for each language studied.
Students wishing to study two languages (‘dual linguists’) should choose Spanish or French as their core language and French or Spanish as one of their optional GCSEs.
The GCSE courses develop and extend the language and topics studied at KS3 and assess all four skills (Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing).
The topics covered in the GCSE course include:
Family, friends, relationships
Physical well-being, mental well-being
Sports, food & drink
The natural world, the environment
Jobs, future plans & careers
Places in town, shopping
Music, TV & film, social media, gaming
Holidays, accommodation, transport, tourist attractions
A GCSE qualification in a Modern Foreign Language is invaluable in today's workplace and can enhance career prospects. Language skills are particularly valued in the fields of journalism, media, law, engineering, business and marketing, ICT, sport and leisure, travel and tourism, customer service, civil service, public services and teaching (UK and abroad).
How is it assessed?
Edexcel GCSE (9-1) French Edexcel GCSE (9-1) Spanish
Students sit separate exams in Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking, each of which is worth 25%. These are all at the end of the course.

pageCache.text:
Year 8 MFL Poetry winners
Four students were selected to represent Heathside in Y8 after having a rigorous competition in class for the best performers.
Yesterday Harry, Orson, Zinedine and Lyla all performed in the St Mary's university MFL Poetry competition. They were up against 55 other students from schools in the area, and had to perform from memory a French or Spanish poem. Harry and Orson performed the French poem “Déjeuner du matin” -the morning breakfast by Jacques Prévert, while Zinedine and Lyla presented “El color de tu piel” - The colour of my skin by Marisa Alonso Santamaría in Spanish.
The event was a wonderful evening, with a packed audience of parents and teachers watching the students bring their poems to life. In the first round, students performed their prepared pieces from memory. Orson impressed the judges by incorporating props, even donning a hat, while Lyla captivated the audience by rapping part of her poem.
In the second round, students were challenged to perform an unseen poem, requiring strong pronunciation, expression and fluency. We are delighted to share that Lyla was awarded Silver in Spanish, and Orson achieved Bronze—a fantastic achievement in such a competitive field.
We are incredibly proud of all four students for showcasing their language skills so confidently and representing Heathside so brilliantly.

Computer Science
Key Stage 3 Computing / Computer Science
Subject Lead: Miss Gill.
Under the new National Curriculum programme of study, ICT has been replaced by Computing so that students are now expected to learn about the use of algorithm-based thinking to develop specific solutions to problems. This still involves the use of packages such as Excel and PowerPoint to generate a requisite product however there is a greater emphasis on coding including the use of block-based models such as Scratch and higher-level programming languages.
At Heathside Walton-on-Thames students’ knowledge will be developed from their starting point at the end of Key Stage 2 through the use of a number of different projects until they will expect to be coding in HTML and Python in Year 9, preparing them for GCSE courses in Computer Science.

Computer Science
What is in the course?
This course aims to give students a deeper insight into how computers and digital products work and is especially helpful for those who see them themselves working in the information industry in the future. Students will learn the basic structure and workings of hardware and how to program using software tools and a high-level programming language
The main topics are:
Component 1: Computer systems
This component will assess:
1.1 Systems architecture
1.2 Memory and storage
1.3 Computer networks, connections, and protocols
1.4 Network security
1.5 Systems software
Component 2: Computational thinking, algorithms, and programming
This component will assess:
2.1 Algorithms
2.2 Programming fundamentals
2.3 Producing robust programs
2.4 Boolean logic
2.5 Programming languages and Integrated Development Environments
How is it assessed:
GCSE Computer Science, Examination board - OCR
The assessment model is of 2 papers. Each paper is 80 marks with a timing of 1 hour 30 minutes.
Paper 1- Component 1: Computer systems
Why consider this course?
This course is ideal for students who have enjoyed programming elements of their Computing study to date and have good mathematical and logical thinking skills. This is a challenging course. Because of the logical nature of the content of this course students will be expected to have achieved at least Grade 9C or above in Mathematics on their Spring report. Experience in the Python programming language is essential.

Drama
Subject Lead: Mrs Haines-Bevan
Key Stage 3 Drama
Subject: Drama Subject Lead: Kathy Haines-Bevan
To provide opportunities for all young people to grow and progress as creative individuals through the acquisition of drama skills, techniques and knowledge learnt through a broad, balanced curriculum. This is a spiral curriculum introducing key concepts in Year 7 and revisiting these throughout KS3.
Our intention is for students to acquire practical skills which enable them to create their own work and to acquire knowledge of the wider world of theatre, its history, cultural developments, influence and purpose in contemporary society. Furthermore, transferable skills such as team-work, self-management, communication, evaluation and leadership are embedded in the practice and theory. Thus, allowing students to reach full potential by developing themselves through all processes of drama including rehearsal, performance and evaluation and to understand how this development can be applied cross-curricular and beyond the classroom. Cumulatively we will be providing young people the opportunities to develop a sense of who they are and who they want to be and the understanding of the power they possess to have a positive impact on their own lives, the lives of others and the community in which they live.
At KS3 all students receive one lesson of Drama per week. Topics change half-termly and each lesson focuses on the acquisition of a new skill or technique and includes information to widen knowledge, build cultural capital and improve application of skills and techniques.

Music
Department vision and curriculum statement
Subject Lead: Mr Deeley
1. Vision for Music
The well-rounded musician at Heathside Walton should:
1. Develop skills in performing and composing music
2. Discover individual musical interests and passions
3. Develop musical grammar through reading and writing music using standard notation
4. Expand cultural awareness through studying different musical traditions
2. Curriculum intent
KS3 curriculum has been developed in consideration of the 3 pillars of music progression:
Throughout this programme of study, students will be exposed to three types of knowledge:
Tacit knowledge – abstract knowledge such as cultural knowledge of music
Procedural knowledge – musical elements and theory applied in performance and composition tasks
Declarative knowledge – musical periods, traditions and performers
The three-year curriculum is split into nine modules, with task-relevant design to reduce cognitive load of procedural knowledge. World Music topics are interwoven within the curriculum (e.g., jazz and computer game music) instead of isolating them from Western Arts music practices. Through interleaved practice, repetition of skills and recalling information, skills are embedded into long-term memory.
The development of this curriculum at KS3 is informed by a critical review of:
Technical
Constructive
Expressive
Model Music Curriculum (2021)
Ofsted Music Research Report (2021)
4. Implementation.
The curriculum is delivered through one fifty-minute lessons per week, across years 7, 8 and 9. Learning an instrument is strongly encouraged and is timetabled through the week as paid 1:1 music lessons.
Music homework is set once per fortnight and alternates between wider listening tests for retrieval practice or creative tasks to extend learning. Students are expected to submit this to Microsoft Teams or bring completed work in exercise books.

Science
Department Vision and Curriculum Statement
Subject: Science Subject Lead: Isabelle Akroyd
Vision for Science
We aspire for Heathside Walton students to leave school with memorable experiences in science lessons and an appreciation of:
Whilst studying science at Heathside, students will:
Curriculum Intent
The KS3 science curriculum builds foundational knowledge in biology, chemistry, and physics while embedding working scientifically skills to provide an enriching practical experience. It has been carefully sequenced to help students integrate new knowledge into existing schemas and develop meaningful links between topics.
Our KS3 science curriculum covers the National Curriculum for Science through topic-based teaching which focuses on Biology, Chemistry or Physics. The scheme integrates digital learning into the classroom and supports teachers to plan and deliver engaging lessons. Best Evidence Science Teaching (BEST) resources are also embedded in the scheme to support teaching of student misconceptions using evidence-based research.
In Year 9, students complete a 12-week transition scheme designed to support their progression into GCSE science. These lessons reinforce essential KS3 learning while extending knowledge in preparation for KS4.
Within the curriculum, students engage with two types of knowledge:
To strengthen disciplinary knowledge, working scientifically lessons are embedded in the curriculum and taught discretely to focus on specific skills. Additional discrete lessons cover science literacy, science in the media, and numeracy skills.
During the summer term, students explore topics beyond the National Curriculum, including local ecosystem studies, the environment, microbes, and disease.
Implementation
The curriculum is delivered through two 50 minute lesson and one 1 hour 40 minute lessons per week, across years 7, 8 and 9.
Science homework is set once per week and is typically retrieval practice homework to support students in their recall of knowledge. Students are usually set a quiz to complete via SENECA or complete pages in their revision guide.

The Science department has the following staff:
Mrs. Akroyd – CAM Science Ms. Sandhu - Deputy CAM Science Mr. Weir – Science Teacher & Head of Learning Year 7 Mrs. Golkari – Physics Subject Lead Dr Small – Science Teacher Mrs. Olorunfunmi – Science Teacher Mrs. Hlebarska – Science Technician Ms. Nazir – Science Technician
The Science Department meets biweekly for subject-specific CPD, collaborative planning, sharing of practical ideas, and moderation of assessments. Teachers and technicians also participate in CPD from organisations such as STEM, SKPT, and CLEAPSS to develop expertise in key departmental focus areas. In addition, teaching staff attend a weekly whole-school CPD session to support the delivery of high-quality lessons in line with the school’s teaching and learning vision. Department members are also affiliated with relevant scientific organisations, including the IOP, RSC, and RSB. • Extracurricular activities and links to the wider world: Students can take part in a range of science-related clubs, including STEM, science, botany, and zoology clubs. The department has also established links with local universities and organisations to broaden students’ understanding of science, research, and career opportunities. Where possible, guest speakers are invited into school to answer questions about careers and inspire students to explore where science can take them. Careers education is embedded in the KS3 curriculum, with each topic linked to a relevant profession. Students also complete summer STEM projects to help connect their classroom learning to real-world applications. ‘Gatsby Benchmark 4’ learning is integrated into the curriculum where applicable, particularly during Careers Week in the summer term.
The department runs an Accelerated Pupil Programme (APP) during the Spring and Summer terms. As part of this programme, students are invited to join a Teams group where they can access an online APP booklet. This booklet provides science activities, recommended places to visit, books and other resources to help students explore science beyond the classroom. Students are also invited to one-off science events during lunch or after school, such as the science of tropical fish or owl pellet dissection. In the classroom, learners are challenged with past exam questions, exposure to higher-level scientific vocabulary and activities that apply scientific concepts to real-world contexts. To support students who need additional help, the department runs an Intervention Pupil Programme (IPP). Following the Autumn Term assessment, students who are significantly below their expected progress are offered targeted support and added to a Teams group. This group provides access to videos, revision resources and quizzes designed to help them improve and reach their target grades in subsequent assessments.
The impact and effectiveness of our curriculum can be evidenced by: 1. Student engagement in science, both in lessons and through extracurricular activities. 2. The quality of student work in exercise books, projects, and assessments. 3. Student progress, as evidenced by our school-wide ‘flightpaths’ assessment model. 4. The development of substantive knowledge as students advance through key stages. 5. The demonstration of disciplinary knowledge and skills. 6. Students’ ability to evaluate their learning and identify areas for improvement. 7. The readiness of KS3 students for GCSE science.

Welcome
I am delighted that you have shown an interest in our school, and hope that the information on our website provides a clear picture of our vision, values, and ethos.
Heathside Walton-on-Thames is an 11-16 free school, which opened in September 2022, serving the communities of Walton on Thames and Molesey. We occupy a brand new, state of the art site on Waterside Drive. When we reach full capacity we will be a school of 900 children, made of five year groups of 180. We believe this means that our school can be one in which all children are known and understood.
All the staff here at Heathside Walton are incredibly proud of the growing community we are building. We believe that through the combination of an outstanding education; an enriching curriculum; and strong pastoral care, wonderful things can be achieved. Our close partnership with our sibling school in Weybridge provides experience, expertise and a proven track record to draw upon. We are delighted to have merged with ECED Trust.
Our children, staff and parent community chose values of Kindness, Resilience and Belonging during our opening term. We try to live these values every day and incorporate them into our shared language wherever we can. We see these values as the key to building a school in which children are safe, happy and can thrive.
Prospective parents and Carers are very welcome to schedule a conversation with me to find out more about our school; this can be done by contacting info@heathsidewalton.org
